claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\), where
\[
N(s,t)=\max\{|s|,|t|,|s-t|\},
\]
the affine-regular hexagonal realization of the real Day--James plane \(\ell_\infty-\ell_1\). For \(1\le p<\infty\), let
\[
C_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(p)}(X)
=
\sup_{(x,y)\ne(0,0)}
\frac{N(x+y)^p+N(x-y)^p}{2^{p-1}\bigl(N(x)^p+N(y)^p\bigr)}.
\]
Then \(C_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(1)}(X)=2\). For every \(p>1\), there is a unique \(\tau_p\in(0,1)\) satisfying
\[
\tau_p^{1-p}-(1+\tau_p)^{1-p}=1,
\]
and
\[
C_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(p)}(X)
=
\frac{1+(1+\tau_p)^p}{2^{p-1}(1+\tau_p^p)}
=
\left(\frac{1+\tau_p}{2\tau_p}\right)^{p-1}.
\]
In the standard unit-sphere parametrization, an extremizer is \(x=(0,1)\), \(y=(1,0)\), with scale parameter \(t=\tau_p\).

correctness.rationale: Homogeneity gives the exact scale reduction. Joint convexity on the product of two hexagonal balls makes a vertex pair extremal for every fixed scale; all relative vertex positions are evaluated. The remaining derivative has the sign of a strictly decreasing function with opposite endpoint signs, giving one global optimizer and the stated algebraic value.
risks: The vertex argument is specific to this polyhedral endpoint.
